mainTopic: Acquiring a rental, and how to measure payment when an item's value depends on how or when it is sold
overview: The amud opens with the end of a ברייתא: a rental is acquired the same ways land is, through money, a document, or taking possession. רב חסדא explains that this means renting land. Then שמואל rules on a robber who takes a cake of fifty dates, worth forty-nine together but fifty one by one. The robber pays an ordinary owner forty-nine but pays הקדש fifty plus a fifth, and a פסוק shows that someone who only damages הקדש pays no fifth. רב ביבי בר אביי asks why the owner can't claim the one-by-one price. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע answers from a משנה that damage is valued as part of the whole. The גמרא then points to another ruling of שמואל, about courtyard rent, that seems to treat ordinary law like הקדש law. רבי יוחנן says שמואל took that ruling back, and רבא's principle shows why. Finally, רבא rules on porters who broke a wine barrel worth more on market day, and the גמרא adds limits on what they owe.

steps.title: A rental is acquired the same ways land is
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by saying that land is acquired through money, a document, or taking possession, and a rental is acquired the same three ways.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as land is acquired through money, a document, or taking possession, so too a rental is acquired through money, a document, or taking possession.
steps.whatsHappening: We are hearing the last words of a ברייתא that started on the previous page. It compares acquiring a rental to acquiring land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Land has three ways of being acquired: כסף, שטר, and חזקה. The ברייתא says a rental works the same way. This raises the question the גמרא asks next.

keyTerms.meaning: Money, here as a way of acquiring
Taking possession by acting like an owner

phrases.english: that land is acquired
through money, a document, or taking possession
so too a rental is acquired
through money, a document, or taking possession.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends a ברייתא carried over from the previous page
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A rental is acquired through כסף, שטר, or חזקה, just like land.

steps.title: Why is rental mentioned here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what kind of rental the ברייתא means, and why it is listed with the ways land is acquired.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rental: what is it doing here?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is puzzled by the word שכירות in the ברייתא and asks what it is about. This sets up רב חסדא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא seems to assume the ברייתא means renting movable items. If so, why would land's ways of acquiring apply? The question asks us to pin down the case.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it doing here? What is its purpose?

phrases.english: Rental, what is its business here?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions a word in the ברייתא just quoted
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of rental the ברייתא is talking about, and why it is acquired like land

steps.title: It means renting land
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא explains that the ברייתא is talking about renting land.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: it means a rental of land.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question. The rental in the ברייתא is a rental of land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we know the rented item is land, it makes sense that renting it works through land's ways of acquiring. The puzzle goes away.
steps.whatToRemember: Renting land is acquired the same three ways as buying land: כסף, שטר, and חזקה.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
a rental of land.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא refers to renting land, so land's ways of acquiring apply.

steps.title: שמואל's case: a stolen cake of fifty dates
steps.stepSummary: שמואל describes a robber who takes a cake of fifty pressed dates. Sold together they bring forty-nine, but sold one by one they bring fifty.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: someone stole a pressed cake of dates from another person, and it has fifty dates. Sold together, they bring fifty minus one. Sold one at a time, they bring fifty.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins with שמואל setting up a case. These are just the facts; his ruling comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key detail is that the same dates have two different values. Together they are worth 49, and one by one they are worth 50. The question will be which value the robber must pay back.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
one who robs
a cake of dates from his fellow
and there are fifty dates in it,
sold together with each other, they sell
for fifty less one,
phrases.notes: The amounts are counted in פרוטות, the smallest coins.

phrases.english: one by one, they sell for fifty.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הַאי מַאן דְּגָזֵיל חֲבִיצָא דְתַמְרֵי מֵחַבְרֵיהּ
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up a stolen item worth 49 sold together and 50 sold one by one.

steps.title: What the robber pays: ordinary owner vs. הקדש vs. a damager
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that the robber pays an ordinary person forty-nine. If the dates belonged to הקדש, he pays fifty plus a fifth. Someone who only damaged הקדש does not pay the fifth.
steps.simpleTranslation: To an ordinary person, he pays fifty minus one. To הקדש, he pays fifty plus the extra fifth. This is not so for a damager, who does not pay the fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives his ruling on the case. The amount depends on who owned the dates.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ordinary owner gets the lower 'together' price of 49. הקדש gets the higher 'one by one' price of 50, plus a חומש, the extra fifth paid for misusing holy property. Step 8 explains why the ordinary owner gets only the 'together' price. A מזיק, someone who damaged הקדש rather than used it, owes no חומש.

keyTerms.meaning: An ordinary person, as opposed to the Temple
The extra fifth paid for misusing holy property

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume the robber always pays the same amount. שמואל gives the ordinary owner the lower price (49) and הקדש the higher price (50).

phrases.english: to an ordinary person, he pays fifty less one,
to the Temple treasury, he pays
fifty and their fifth,
which is not so with one who damages,
who does not pay the fifth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling for the case just described
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ordinary owner: 49. הקדש: 50 plus a fifth. A damager of הקדש pays no fifth.

steps.title: The פסוק that frees a damager from the fifth
steps.stepSummary: The source for the damager rule: the פסוק speaks about one who 'eats' holy food, which leaves out someone who only damages it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the master said: 'And a man who eats holy food'; this leaves out a damager.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to back up the last part of שמואל's ruling, that a מזיק pays no fifth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק requiring the fifth uses the word 'eats', meaning a person who benefits from הקדש. Someone who only damaged it did not eat or benefit, so he is left out of the fifth.
steps.whatToRemember: The fifth is only for someone who uses or eats הקדש, not for someone who only damages it.

phrases.english: as the master said:
"And a man, if he eats holy food"
leaving out one who damages.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר מָר: וְאִישׁ כִּי יֹאכַל קֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the damager rule in the previous step
steps.raayaObject: That a damager of הקדש does not pay the fifth
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 22:14, 'ואיש כי יאכל קודש', which limits the fifth to one who eats

steps.title: Why should the ordinary owner get only forty-nine?
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי בר אביי challenges שמואל. The ordinary owner should be able to say he would have sold the dates one by one for fifty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי בר אביי objected: why does the robber pay an ordinary person only fifty minus one? Let the owner tell him: I would have sold them one at a time!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ביבי בר אביי attacks the first part of שמואל's ruling, the 49 paid to an ordinary owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner could have earned 50 by selling the dates singly. So why should the robber pay only the lower 'together' price? The challenge asks why the ordinary owner is not treated like הקדש and given the higher value.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged it, raised an objection

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב בִּיבִי בַּר אַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rav Beivai bar Abaye objected to it:
to an ordinary person, why does he pay
fifty less one?
Let him say to him:
phrases.notes: The owner is speaking to the robber.

phrases.english: I, one by one,
would have sold them?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב בִּיבִי בַּר אַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first part of שמואל's ruling
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that an ordinary owner receives only 49
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The owner could have sold the dates one by one for 50, so the robber should owe him 50.

steps.title: Damage is measured as part of the larger unit
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע cites a משנה: when an animal damages a field, the court values the damage as part of a בית סאה. In the same way, the date-cake is valued whole, at forty-nine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said: We learned in a משנה, 'They appraise a בית סאה in that field.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers רב ביבי's challenge from step 7. He shows from a משנה that the owner cannot demand the higher piece-by-piece price.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the damaged garden bed is not valued alone. It is valued as part of a larger area, which gives a smaller payment. The date-cake is the same: it is valued as one whole cake, worth forty-nine, and not as fifty separate dates.

keyTerms.meaning: They appraise (the court estimates the value)
An area of land large enough to plant one סאה of seed

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said:
We learned: 'They appraise a beit se'a in that field.'
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in בבא קמא about an animal that ate from a field. The damaged spot is valued as part of a bigger piece of land.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב ביבי בר אביי's challenge to שמואל
steps.terutzResolutionType: Support from a משנה showing that damage is valued as part of the larger whole
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The owner could claim the higher piece-by-piece value of fifty
steps.terutzMaskana: Damages are measured by the value of the whole unit, so the robber pays forty-nine

steps.title: Does שמואל really separate ordinary rules from הקדש rules?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether שמואל really holds that payment to an ordinary person differs from payment to הקדש. It sets up a challenge from a משנה in מעילה about taking a stone or beam of הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does this mean שמואל holds that the law for an ordinary person is not like the law for הקדש? But we learned: If someone took a stone or beam from הקדש, he has not committed מעילה. If he gave it to his friend, he has committed מעילה and his friend has not. If he built it into his house, he has not committed מעילה until he lives under it and gets a פרוטה's worth of benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a challenge against שמואל and quotes a משנה. This משנה is the setup for the next step, where שמואל's own words about it are brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 5, שמואל made ordinary payment (forty-nine) different from הקדש payment (fifty). The גמרא suspects that שמואל elsewhere treats the two the same. The משנה about living under a הקדש beam will be the base for that other statement of שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Most High': property belonging to הקדש
He committed מעילה, wrongful use of holy property
The value of a פרוטה, the smallest coin

phrases.english: Is this to say that Shmuel holds

phrases.aramaic: דִּין הֶדְיוֹט לָאו כְּדִין גָּבוֹהַּ דָּמֵי?
phrases.english: that the law of a common person is not like the law of the Most High?
phrases.notes: 'The Most High' means הקדש, property that belongs to the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn: If one took a stone or a beam
from הקדש, he has not committed me'ila,
if he gave it to his friend, he has committed me'ila,
and his friend has not committed me'ila.
If he built it into his house, he has not committed me'ila
until he lives under it for the value of a peruta.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּסָבַר שְׁמוּאֵל דִּין הֶדְיוֹט לָאו כְּדִין גָּבוֹהַּ דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a new challenge against the principle behind שמואל's ruling
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling in step 5 that an ordinary person gets forty-nine while הקדש gets fifty
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל elsewhere learns ordinary law from הקדש law, which suggests the two are alike

steps.title: שמואל learns rent for a courtyard from the הקדש beam
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו reports that שמואל learned from this משנה that one who lives in another's courtyard without permission must pay rent. So שמואל does compare ordinary law to הקדש law.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו was sitting before רבי יוחנן, and he said in the name of שמואל: This teaches that one who lives in his friend's courtyard without his knowledge must pay him rent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its challenge. It shows that שמואל himself learned an ordinary-person rule from the הקדש משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Living under a הקדש beam counts as benefit that must be paid for. שמואל applied the same idea to an ordinary person's courtyard. That treats ordinary law like הקדש law, which seems to contradict step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This teaches': a lesson drawn from a source

phrases.aramaic: וִיתֵיב רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Abbahu was sitting before Rabbi Yoḥanan,
and he was sitting and saying in the name of Shmuel:
This teaches: One who lives in his friend's courtyard

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא מִדַּעְתּוֹ צָרִיךְ לְהַעֲלוֹת לוֹ שָׂכָר.
phrases.english: without his knowledge must pay him rent.

steps.triggerLanguage: וִיתֵיב רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge by showing how שמואל used the משנה
steps.raayaObject: That שמואל treats ordinary law like הקדש law
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's statement, reported by רבי אבהו, learning courtyard rent from the משנה in מעילה
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's date-cake ruling (step 5), which treats an ordinary person differently from הקדש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל himself learned courtyard rent for an ordinary person from the משנה about living under a הקדש beam, so he does treat ordinary law like הקדש law. That contradicts his date-cake ruling.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: שמואל took that ruling back
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that שמואל retracted the courtyard ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: שמואל retracted that ruling.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן settles the contradiction. He says שמואל took back one of the two rulings, so there is no clash.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once one ruling is dropped, שמואל has no contradiction left. רבי יוחנן says שמואל dropped 'that' one, the courtyard rent ruling, so the date-cake ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He retracted; he took back his opinion

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said to him:
Shmuel retracted from that one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הֲדַר בֵּיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל מֵהַהִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in steps 9-10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Retraction: one of the two conflicting rulings was withdrawn
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל holds both rulings, and they contradict each other

steps.title: How do we know which ruling he took back?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know שמואל retracted the courtyard ruling. Maybe he retracted the date-cake ruling instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that he retracted that ruling? Maybe he retracted this one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רבי יוחנן's answer. It asks why we assume the courtyard ruling was dropped and not the date-cake ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A retraction removes the contradiction either way. So the גמרא needs a reason to pick which ruling was dropped. 'This one' means the date-cake ruling of step 5.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that he retracted from that one;
perhaps he retracted from this one?
phrases.notes: 'This one' is שמואל's ruling about the stolen cake of dates.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִמַּאי דְּמֵהַהִיא הֲדַר בֵּיהּ דִּלְמָא מֵהָא הֲדַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions which ruling רבי יוחנן's retraction applies to
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Proof that the courtyard ruling, and not the date-cake ruling, is the one שמואל dropped

steps.title: The courtyard ruling fails because of רבא's principle
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שמואל must have dropped the courtyard ruling. As רבא teaches, using הקדש without permission is like using an ordinary person's property with permission, so the courtyard case cannot be learned from הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, he retracted that one, as רבא said. For רבא said: הקדש without permission is like an ordinary person with permission.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the courtyard ruling was the one dropped. That ruling was built on a weak comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הקדש really belongs to ה׳, so using it always counts as if done with the owner's permission. Using it is therefore like using an ordinary person's property with his knowledge, where he can expect to be paid. So the הקדש משנה cannot teach about living in someone's courtyard without his knowledge, and the courtyard ruling has no source.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל keeps his date-cake ruling (pay forty-nine to an ordinary person). He drops the courtyard rent ruling, because using הקדש is always treated like using property with the owner's permission.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying הקדש gets less protection. He is saying that, since הקדש belongs to ה׳, it always counts as used 'with the owner's knowledge.' That is why it cannot be compared to a case without the owner's knowledge.
steps.whyThisMatters: It explains why rules about benefit from הקדש cannot simply be copied over to cases of using an ordinary person's property without his knowledge.

phrases.english: No, it is from that one that he retracted,
in accordance with Rava. As Rava said:
Consecrated property used without knowledge
is like a common person's property used with knowledge.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמואל retracted the courtyard ruling, because רבא's principle shows הקדש cannot teach about use without the owner's knowledge
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: שמואל's date-cake ruling stands. The courtyard rent ruling was withdrawn.

steps.title: Porters who broke a wine barrel before market day
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that porters who broke a shopkeeper's wine barrel may repay with a barrel of wine on market day, but on other days they must pay five, the market-day price.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says: Porters broke a shopkeeper's barrel of wine. On market day it sells for five, and on other days for four. If they pay him back on market day, they can give him a barrel of wine. If they pay him back on other days, they must give him five.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רבא about how much porters must pay for a broken wine barrel when its price depends on the day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shopkeeper lost the chance to sell the wine on market day for five. On market day, a replacement barrel lets him get that full five himself, so it is enough. On other days a barrel is only worth four, so the porters must pay the full five he lost.

keyTerms.meaning: Market day, when prices are higher

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the porters always owe only what the wine is worth on the day they pay. The loss being paid for is the five the shopkeeper would have gotten on market day.

phrases.english: Rava says:
These porters who broke
a barrel of wine belonging to a shopkeeper,
which on market day sells for five,
and on other days sells for four.
If they repay him on market day,
they repay him with a barrel of wine,
phrases.notes: He can sell that barrel right away for five, so he loses nothing.

phrases.english: on other days, they repay him five.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הָנֵי שָׁקוֹלָאֵי דִּתְבַרוּ חָבִיתָא דְּחַמְרָא לְחַנְווֹאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the discussion of שמואל and הקדש, the גמרא brings another ruling, this one from רבא, about compensation whose value depends on timing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Damages for a broken barrel are measured by the market-day price of five. On market day, a replacement barrel covers this. On other days, five must be paid.

steps.title: Limit: only if the shopkeeper had no other wine to sell
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits רבא's ruling. Payment of five applies only if the shopkeeper had no other wine to sell that market day. If he had other wine and didn't sell it, the porters did not cost him the market-day sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: We only said this when he had no other wine to sell. But if he had wine to sell, he should have sold it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a limit to רבא's ruling, explaining when the porters really owe the higher market-day price.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra one coin is owed only because the porters made the shopkeeper miss a market-day sale. If he had other wine and still didn't sell it, his missed profit is not their fault. In that case he gets only the regular value.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this when, a phrase that limits a ruling
He should have, it was up to him

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the higher payment is for a real lost sale that the damager caused, not an automatic penalty.

phrases.english: And we said this only
where he did not have wine to sell,
phrases.notes: He means other wine besides the broken barrel, which he could have sold that market day.

phrases.english: but if he had wine to sell,
then he should have sold it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא הֲוָה לֵיהּ חַמְרָא לְזַבּוֹנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It narrows רבא's ruling from Step 14 to the case where the shopkeeper had no other wine available.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The market-day price is owed only if the broken barrel actually cost the shopkeeper a market-day sale, meaning he had no other wine to sell.

steps.title: Subtract the shopkeeper's saved effort and tapping costs
steps.stepSummary: When the porters pay five, they may subtract the value of the selling effort and the cost of tapping the barrel, since the shopkeeper was spared these.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they subtract from what they pay him the value of his effort and the cost of opening the barrel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second limit: the five that the porters pay is reduced by the costs the shopkeeper no longer has.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To earn five on market day, the shopkeeper would have had to work at selling and pay to open the barrel. Since the porters are paying him the money directly, he saved those costs. So those amounts are taken off.

keyTerms.meaning: Tapping, opening a barrel to pour out the wine

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's rule: damages are measured by the shopkeeper's real market-day loss. This applies only if he had no other wine to sell, and his saved effort and tapping costs are subtracted.

phrases.english: And they deduct for him the payment for his effort
and the cost of tapping the barrel.
phrases.notes: Selling the wine would have meant paying to tap the barrel. He never had that cost here, so it comes off.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְנַכֵּי לֵיהּ אֲגַר טִירְחֵיהּ וּדְמֵי בַּרְזַנְיָיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It adds a second limit to רבא's ruling, adjusting the amount owed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the five paid, the porters deduct the value of the shopkeeper's selling effort and the cost of tapping the barrel.
